title: मुक्तक सिद्धान्त र केही प्रयोग
nepali: कलाका दुई भदे मध्ये ललित कलाको एक शाखाका रुपमा साहित्य पर्दछ । साहित्यका पनि विभिन्न भदे मध्ये कविता विधाको छोटो छरितो र लघतु म रचनालाई मुक्तक भनिन्छ । साहित्य कला,संस्कृति समाजका प्रतिबिम्ब हुन् । समाज जे जस्तो छ त्यस्तै साहित्य सिर्जना हुन्छ । कुनै व्यक्ति, वस्तु र घटनाले सजर्क को मन र मस्तिष्कलाई तरङ्गित पार्दछ र त्यसमा अनुभव र अनुभूतिका साथै कल्पनाले रङ्गाएर साहित्य सिर्जना गरिन्छ । मुक्त अर्थात् बन्धन नभएको स्वतन्त्र रुपमा रचना गरिने कविताको संक्षिप्त स्वरुप नै मुक्तक हो । यस लेखमा मुक्तकको परिचय, परिभाषा, विशेषता, वर्गीकरणका साथै मुक्तकका विभिन्न उपभेदमध्ये रुबाइको संक्षिप्त परिचय, रदीफ, काफियाका, साथै केही रुबाई शैलीमा रचना गरिएका मुक्तकलाई प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ ।
american_english: Literature falls as one branch of the fine arts among the two divisions of art. Among the various divisions of literature too, the short, brief and concise composition of the poetic genre is called a muktak. Literature, art and culture are reflections of society. Whatever society is like, literature is created in just that way. Some person, object or event stirs the mind and brain of the creator, and in that, experience and feeling together with imagination colour it, and literature is created. 'Mukt' means free, that is, without bondage; the short form of a poem composed in a free manner is a muktak. In this article, the introduction, definition, characteristics and classification of the muktak, as well as, among the various sub-types of the muktak, a brief introduction to the rubai, radif and kafiya, and some muktaks composed in the rubai style, have been presented.

Just as society is, so literature is created. A person, object or event stirs the mind and brain of the creator, and in that, experience and feeling, along with imagination, colour it, and literature is created. 'Mukt' means free, that is, without bondage; the concise form of a poem composed in a free way is a muktak. In this article, an account of the introduction, definition, characteristics and classification of the muktak has been given, and among the various sub-types of the muktak, a brief introduction to the rubai, radif and kafiya, together with certain muktaks composed in the rubai style, has been presented.
